title: Donald Trump Says US Is Working on ‘Larger-Scale’ Ukraine-Russia Ceasefire
html:
US President Donald Trump stated that Washington is seeking to expand earlier localized humanitarian arrangements between Ukraine and Russia into a “larger-scale” ceasefire, crediting First Lady Melania Trump for playing a key role in previous evacuation efforts.

Speaking in an interview with Fox News, Trump pointed to past localized pauses that allowed civilians to evacuate populated areas, suggesting that the White House is working to replicate and broaden that model without providing specific operational details.

“It was wonderful. It was a truce. People were evacuated from cities and populated areas, which probably saved their lives. Now we are working on a larger-scale version of this,” Trump said.

The president praised Melania Trump’s involvement in humanitarian initiatives between Ukraine and the US, noting her cooperation with officials and intermediaries engaged in those efforts before adding: “Now we are moving to a broader format.”

Melania Trump’s Christmas truce wish

Trump’s comments follow an interview with Fox News on Friday, Nov. 20, in which Melania Trump expressed hope that Ukraine and Russia could reach a new ceasefire agreement by Christmas, stating that negotiations are underway and could produce rapid results if both sides are willing.

Concurrently, President Volodymyr Zelensky released an updated list on Saturday, Nov. 21, of temporarily occupied settlements in the southern Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions that Kyiv has submitted to Ukraine’s Human Rights Ombudsman and the US for potential civilian humanitarian evacuation missions, building on an earlier localized evacuation in Oleshky.

In the Kherson region, Ukraine proposed humanitarian missions in Radensk, Kostohryzove, Hola Prystan, Stara Zburivka, Nova Zburivka, Hladkivka, Velyki Kopani, Kardashynka, and Velyka Kardashynka, alongside Maiachka, Zlatopil, Dniprorudne, Kamianske, Verkhnia Krynytsia, and Vasylivka in the Zaporizhzhia region.

Previously, Zelensky rejected a separate Russian proposal for a “humanitarian operation” in the contested eastern city of Kostiantynivka in Donetsk region as a military ploy to rotate troops and advance toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk.

Broader diplomatic backdrop in Washington and Europe

The White House’s push for a broader truce coincides with Financial Times reporting that the Trump administration is seeking to broker a settlement by early January, ahead of incoming Democratic majorities taking control of both chambers of the US Congress following the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have pressed the timeline across recent meetings in Abu Dhabi, Moscow, Dublin, and Berlin, raising concerns in Kyiv that Ukraine could face pressure to accept unfavorable terms.

On Saturday, Zelensky stated that the next round of four-party peace talks involving Ukraine, Europe, Russia, and the US must deliver concrete outcomes, an “all-for-all” prisoner exchange, and real steps toward ending the war, noting that the timing depends on Washington finalizing the agenda while Moscow attempts to stall.
